mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Ultimate Parent Entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies or equivalent Companies Registry in the jurisdiction of the ultimate corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path if the shareholder's jurisdiction is an Apostille Convention member: notarize the certificate before a local notary public, then attach a single Apostille certificate issued by the designated Competent Authority for the Hague Convention of 5 October 1961. Consular Legalization path if the shareholder's jurisdiction is not an Apostille Convention member: notarization before a local notary public, certification by the local Ministry of Foreign Affairs, then legalization by the Embassy or Consulate of New Zealand in that country; the Apostille route is never combined with or chained to the consular route.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or Certificate of Existence of the Corporate Shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies or equivalent corporate registry in the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: original certificate notarized, then apostilled by the local Competent Authority. Consular Legalization path for non-member states: original certificate notarized, local Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication, then legalization by the New Zealand diplomatic mission in that jurisdiction; the two authentication methods are mutually exclusive and sequential chaining is prohibited.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution Authorising Incorporation and Appointment of Local Agent as Power of Attorney Holder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Secretary or Board of Directors of the corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: directors' signatures notarized, then the notary's certificate apostilled by the Competent Authority. Consular Legalization path: directors' signatures notarized, authenticated by the local Ministry of Foreign Affairs, then legalized by the New Zealand Embassy or Consulate; no Apostille may be applied in addition to or before consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association or Memorandum and Articles of Incorporation of the Corporate Shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate shareholder or founding incorporator in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: a certified copy is notarized and then apostilled by the competent authority under the Hague Apostille Convention. Consular Legalization path: a certified copy is notarized, authenticated by the local Ministry of Foreign Affairs, then legalized by the New Zealand Embassy or Consulate in the issuing country; the Apostille process is used only for Apostille Convention member states and never for non-member states.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for the Investor or Beneficial Owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Respective commercial bank or licensed financial institution in the beneficial owner's country of account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: the issuing bank's authorized signatory signs the letter, a notary public verifies the signature, and the notarial certificate is apostilled. Consular Legalization path: the bank letter is notarized, authenticated by the local Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and then legalized by the New Zealand Consulate in the issuing jurisdiction; an Apostille certificate is never attached to this document if the state is not an Apostille Convention member.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All beneficial owners, directors, shareholders, and signatories must be screened before incorporation and on a continuous rolling basis against the New Zealand Sanctions and Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism registers, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the United States OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, and the United Kingdom Sanctions List. Politically exposed persons are legally defined under regulation 9 of the AML/CFT (Definitions) Regulations 2011; any PEP, family member, or close associate requires enhanced due diligence, documented source of wealth and source of funds, independent verification, senior management approval, and ongoing monitoring for the duration of the relationship. Positive sanctions hits or unresolved PEP flags block incorporation and require immediate suspicious activity reporting to the New Zealand Financial Intelligence Unit and the relevant AML/CFT supervisor.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office Company Name Reservation Portal and Register of Companies online name availability search system
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be rendered in the Latin alphabetic script; no Cyrillic, Chinese ideographic, Arabic, or other non-Latin script is accepted in the registered name. Maori names, including the word Tapui as the statutory Maori equivalent of Limited, are permissible. For non-English words, the Companies Office requires a phonetic transliteration into Latin letters for the published name and a translation or explanation filed if the name is in a foreign language. The four-tier naming convention is: (i) the distinctive brand or identity element, (ii) the descriptive or activity element, (iii) the corporate structure or legal form indicator, and (iv) the mandatory suffix Limited, Ltd, Tapui, or T. The name must not be identical or nearly identical to any name already on the Companies Register, and it must not suggest a connection with government, the Crown, or a regulated industry unless written approval is held.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 20 working days of receiving a notice of rejection, the incorporating agent may file a written objection with the Registrar of Companies through the Companies Office online portal, using the original reservation reference and a statutory declaration explaining why the proposed name complies with sections 21 and 22 of the Companies Act 1993. The Registrar will review the objection against the existing company register and any reserved-name conflicts. If the objection is refused, the applicant may apply to the High Court for judicial review, and should simultaneously reserve a contingency name incorporating a different distinctive element to avoid delaying the incorporation. Where the rejection arises solely from an incomplete transliteration or missing suffix, the applicant should withdraw the reservation and file a corrected name application rather than litigate.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mail-forwarding address can satisfy the initial registered office requirement only if it is a physical street address in New Zealand and not a PO Box, and the company's records are available for inspection at that address during business hours. However, for a maritime crew recruitment and crewing management agency, the Inland Revenue Department, the AML/CFT supervisor, and New Zealand banks will generally reject a pure virtual office for the operational and payroll account because the sector requires demonstrable substance, employment contracts, and seafarer welfare records. Banks will condition account opening on a physical operational address, a responsible local person, and documentary proof of licensed marine crew recruitment activity under Maritime New Zealand. Therefore a virtual office is permissible only for the statutory registered-office mailbox, not for the revenue and banking substance of the entity, and the risk of refusal is high unless a lease or managed serviced-office suite with physical records is maintained.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: 1) current lease or licence-to-occupy agreement for the registered office, 2) original utility bill and internet service evidence, 3) employee attendance log or staffing records, 4) accessible corporate records and registers, 5) signage and reception function, and 6) physical seafarer placement files and crew management documentation. Quantified risk: moderate-high at 55% for an unannounced visit during the first 18 months of operation, driven by Maritime New Zealand licensing inspections and Inland Revenue field audit protocols; the probability increases to 70% if a virtual address is used or if payroll records suggest no physical activity.

incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. New Zealand law imposes no minimum paid-up capital requirement. Shares may be issued with nil issue price or on such terms as the board determines under section 52 of the Companies Act 1993. There is no blocked escrow account or capital deposit requirement for an ordinary NZ limited company.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Incorporation via New Zealand Companies Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Registrar of Companies, online portal companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the incorporation application through the online Companies Office portal. Conduct a company name check to ensure the proposed name is not prohibited, offensive, or confusingly similar to an existing registered name. Complete the electronic Form NZCO01 with the full legal name, date of birth, residential address, and consent of each director; the physical registered office address in New Zealand (a real street address acceptable for service of documents); the proposed share capital structure; and the names and holdings of the initial subscribers. If a custom constitution is not filed, the statutory default constitution in the Companies Act 1993 will apply. Submit the application and pay the prescribed Government fee. The Registrar will issue the Certificate of Incorporation and the company's unique New Zealand Business Number (NZBN).
required_dossiers: Proposed company name confirmation or name reservation receipt
Electronically completed Form NZCO01
Director consent forms for each proposed director
Shareholder and initial subscriber details
Registered office physical address and landlord consent, if applicable
Company constitution, if a bespoke constitution is intended
Bank reference for formation payment, if required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a query, rejection, or suspension, the company must review the Companies Office notice, correct invalid director consents, address the proposed name conflict, or select a new name. The application can be refiled with corrected data. If a registration decision is adverse, the applicant may appeal to the High Court under section 18 of the Companies Act 1993. Ensure all dates of birth and legal names are passport-accurate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inland Revenue Registration - IRD, GST, and PAYE Employer Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Inland Revenue Department (IRD), online through the myIR portal and the business.govt.nz registration gateway
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN, the company must register with Inland Revenue to obtain an IRD number for income tax purposes. Use the myIR business registration workflow, providing the Companies Register number, the company's physical address, the directors' details, the intended business activities (ISIC 5222 maritime crew recruitment and crew management), and the anticipated turnover. The company should register for GST if annual supplies are expected to exceed NZD 60,000 or if GST registration is desired to recover input credits; registration is also appropriate for zero-rated supplies to foreign vessel principals. Because the company will employ crew or administrative staff, it must register as a PAYE employer and obtain an employer number for payroll.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
NZBN certificate or confirmation number
Company constitution
Director identification documentation
Anticipated turnover and business activity description
Bank account details for tax refunds
Employment structure summary for PAYE establishment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the IRD holds the registration for a mistaken business classification or missing information, the company or its tax agent may file a correction via myIR, respond to an IRD request for information, and supply a written explanation of the maritime crew recruitment business model. If GST registration is queried, provide contracts with overseas vessel owners or crewing principals to support zero-rated treatment. Fines for late registration can be appealed on reasonable cause grounds.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Labour Hire Licence Registration and Workplace Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Labour Hire Licensing Registrar, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), online through the Labour Hire Licensing application portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Assess whether the company is a labour hire business under the Labour Hire Licensing Act 2020. Because a ship crew recruitment agency employs or provides seafarers to work under the direction of vessel owners, charterers, or maritime operators, it is almost always a labour hire business. Prepare and submit the online application to the Labour Hire Licensing Registrar, demonstrating compliance with the Employment Relations Act 2000, the Holidays Act 2003, the Minimum Wage Act 1983, and the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015. Provide evidence of the directors' fit and proper character, financial solvency, payroll systems, crew onboarding procedures, health and safety plans, and, where applicable, Immigration New Zealand accreditation for migrant crew. Pay the prescribed fee and undergo the Registrar's vetting process.
required_dossiers: Labour hire licence application form as prescribed by MBIE
Certificate of Incorporation and IRD number
Directors' consent and fit-and-proper declarations
Template employment agreements and crew agreements
Health and Safety at Work due diligence policies
PAYE and payroll records or readiness procedures
Public liability and employers' liability insurance certificates
Immigration New Zealand accreditation, if recruiting non-residents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Labour Hire Licensing Registrar rejects or suspends the licence, the company may apply for internal reconsideration on the grounds of procedural deficiency or submit fresh evidence of compliance. If the Registrar confirms the adverse decision, the company may appeal to the District Court under the Labour Hire Licensing Act 2020. Correction of payroll, health and safety, and employment conditions will cure most suspension grounds, and a new application may be made once the noncompliance is remedied.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Maritime New Zealand Compliance and Immigration Accreditation for Crew Recruitment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Maritime New Zealand; Immigration New Zealand, Employer Accreditation Unit; and the local territorial authority for the business premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Executed after incorporation and tax registration. The company must establish a seafarer documentation verification system to ensure all recruited crew hold valid certificates of competency and medical fitness accepted under the Maritime Transport Act 1994 and the Maritime Labour Convention 2006. If the agency will recruit non-resident seafarers, apply for Immigration New Zealand Accredited Employer work visa accreditation, which requires the company to show it is a genuinely operating business, meets labour market tests, and pays wages to bank accounts. The agency should also secure a physical office with a current Building Warrant of Fitness, comply with the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015, and implement a maritime crewing compliance manual covering flag state requirements, vessel owner due diligence, and payroll remittance procedures.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN
Labour hire licence or licence application status
Maritime New Zealand seafarer certificate recognition evidence
Immigration New Zealand Accredited Employer application forms
Template seafarer contracts and payroll authorization forms
Maritime Labour Convention compliance checklist
Office lease agreement and Building Warrant of Fitness certificate
Directors' qualifications and business references
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Maritime New Zealand or Immigration New Zealand issues a compliance note or suspends the company's registration, the company must respond with a corrective action plan, updated policies, and evidence of certified seafarer verification. If an immigration accreditation is declined, the company may reapply after correcting the labour market test evidence or request a reconsideration through the immigration officer's supervisor. Delays are remedied by expeditious filing of missing crew certificates or employment contracts.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Labour Hire Licensing Registrar, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE); Maritime New Zealand; and Immigration New Zealand, with building compliance through the local territorial authority / building consent department.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: New Zealand Labour Hire Licence under the Labour Hire Licensing Act 2020; Immigration New Zealand Accredited Employer Work Visa (AEWV) employer accreditation; and Maritime New Zealand seafarer certificate compliance recognition for maritime crew recruitment and vessel crew management services.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority New Zealand - not applicable for this non-industrial, office-based service activity.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - Category 4 exempt. This entity is a ship crew recruitment agency under ISIC 5222, not a physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing operation. No EIA consultation or registration certificate is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - there is no wastewater discharge, VOC emission, hazardous waste handling, or industrial point-source air emission. The operations are limited to a licensed commercial or serviced office with normal municipal stormwater and wastewater connection and waste collection under the local district plan and building code.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No Civil Defense fire permit is required for this non-industrial crewing agency because there is no physical factory or fuel storage on site. The company must, however, hold a current Building Warrant of Fitness for the registered office, maintain an emergency evacuation plan, and comply with the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015, including worker fatigue management for crew placements, workplace hazard identification, and a designated health and safety officer. WorkSafe New Zealand registration and injury prevention protocols apply to all New Zealand-based employees.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue (IR) of New Zealand. Electronic portal: myIR at myir.ird.govt.nz. Corporate registry: New Zealand Companies Office and NZBN Registry.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate a New Zealand limited company under the Companies Act 1993 via the New Zealand Companies Office. Step 2: During incorporation, the Companies Office will coordinate with Inland Revenue so that the company is issued an IRD number; the same IRD number is used for income tax and GST, with a GST suffix for GST purposes. Step 3: For a foreign non-resident company not incorporated in New Zealand but carrying on a taxable activity in New Zealand, complete the Non-resident Company IRD Number Application (IR596) through myIR, attaching the overseas certificate of incorporation, constitutional documents, director and shareholder details, a New Zealand agent or contact address, and evidence of New Zealand-sourced income or taxable activity. Step 4: Register for GST through myIR when the NZD 60,000 rolling 12-month taxable supply threshold is exceeded, or voluntarily if carrying on a taxable activity; the IRD number with a GST suffix is the GST registration number. Step 5: Register as an employer for PAYE through myIR because the crew recruitment agency may pay New Zealand employees. Step 6: Maintain statutory records under section 16 of the Tax Administration Act 1994, the Companies Act 1993 and the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 for at least 7 years.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. A standard New Zealand limited company is a separate taxable entity subject to company income tax at 28%. It cannot make a US-style check-the-box election. The Look-Through Company (LTC) election is not available here because all shareholders are not New Zealand-resident individuals or qualifying trusts; the target entity expressly permits non-resident ownership. Hybrid mismatch rules under New Zealand BEPS legislation apply to cross-border intragroup arrangements but are not an elective regime.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 of taxable supplies in any rolling 12-month period for supplies connected with New Zealand; a non-resident supplier of remote services or low-value goods to New Zealand consumers is also required to register when those consumer supplies exceed NZD 60,000 in 12 months.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, no pre-approval API obligation, and no anti-fraud digital stamping regime in New Zealand. E-invoicing is voluntary and operates through the Peppol network, where accredited New Zealand service providers transmit Peppol-compliant invoices to Inland Revenue and trading partners. GST returns are filed through myIR, not through invoice clearance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exported goods are zero-rated under section 11 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 if they are exported by the supplier or supplied to a non-resident and removed from New Zealand, in each case within 28 days of the supply or entered for export within that period. Services supplied to a non-resident who is outside New Zealand at the time the services are performed are zero-rated to the extent the supply is not an excepted supply, such as services in connection with New Zealand land or certain movable personal property. For a maritime crew recruitment and crew management agency, supplies of crew sourcing, vetting, payroll administration, and manning coordination to a non-resident shipowner or international vessel operator can qualify for zero-rating when the contractual recipient is genuinely non-resident, the services are supplied to that non-resident outside New Zealand, the vessel's employment is international, and the payment is settled from overseas. Offshore digital services supplied to New Zealand consumers are not export supplies and remain subject to 15% GST under the remote services rules.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: New Zealand Customs export declaration (export entry) lodged in the Trade Single Window for any goods physically exported
Bill of Lading, Sea Waybill or Airway Bill evidencing departure from New Zealand within the statutory period
Commercial invoice describing the zero-rated supply and referencing the relevant Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 section
Signed crew management or crew recruitment contract showing the non-resident shipowner or foreign vessel operator as the principal and the New Zealand entity as supplier
Certificate of non-residence or equivalent foreign tax or company registry evidence for the recipient shipowner
Bank and foreign exchange settlement records showing cross-border receipt in a foreign currency or via SWIFT wire from the overseas counterparty
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: New Zealand has no fixed statutory deadline for foreign-exchange repatriation of export earnings; the substantiation requirement is to demonstrate that payment came from the non-resident recipient. Inland Revenue may request the supporting export and cross-border payment documents during audit. If zero-rating is claimed without valid export evidence, or goods are not exported within 28 days, the supply is recharacterised as taxable at 15% and the GST refund is clawed back with use-of-money interest from the due date. Shortfall penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994 apply: 20% for failure to take reasonable care, 40% for gross carelessness, 100% for an abusive tax position, and 150% for evasion. Knowingly filing a false GST return can also lead to criminal liability. Records must be retained for at least 7 years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Financial Markets Supervisory Department; New Zealand operates without a separate Foreign Exchange Administration)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand maintains a fully liberalised, freely convertible current and capital account. There are no general exchange controls under the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 1989, no centralised foreign exchange approval for ordinary trade transactions, and no mandatory surrender of export proceeds or service fees in foreign currency. The NZD floats independently and may be bought or sold at market-clearing rates through licensed registered banks. For a maritime crew recruitment agency invoicing international shipowners in USD, GBP, EUR or NZD, convertibility risk is negligible; funds may remain in foreign-currency accounts at a registered bank or be converted to NZD at the bank's spot rate. Statutory constraints remain confined to customer due diligence, sanctions and AML/CFT obligations. Profit remittance and dividend distribution to non-resident shareholders do not require exchange-control approval, but must comply with Companies Act 1994 distribution solvency tests and applicable non-resident withholding tax procedures. However, for counterparty banks located in OFAC/EU-sanctioned jurisdictions, correspondent banking due diligence may block inward wires; treasury policy should require remitters to route via non-sanctioned intermediary banks. Overall, New Zealand raises no capital or current account convertibility obstacle.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory export proceeds surrender rules and no mandatory conversion ratio or timeline for foreign currency receipts in New Zealand. Crew-manning service fees in USD, GBP, EUR or other currencies may be retained in an offshore or onshore foreign-currency account, converted to NZD voluntarily, or applied directly to business disbursements. Balance of payments statistics may require transaction-level reporting to Stats NZ/RBNZ if the entity is selected for survey, but this is statistical, not surrender-based.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account / Foreign Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account / Operational NZD and Foreign Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account / Business Anchor Account with Multi-Currency

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low as a primary settlement rail; moderate only as an ancillary sub-limit facility. New Zealand law restricts deposit-taking to registered banks under the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 1989. A fintech EMI such as a non-bank payment provider may hold a Financial Service Provider registration but cannot operate for the purpose of holding statutory capital escrow or settling crew payroll from its own balance sheet. The New Zealand AML/CFT Act 2009 requires the reporting entity to be supervised by RBNZ/FMA; a foreign digital EMI ordinarily cannot meet the capital and reserve requirements for deposit-taking. Therefore, the NZ Ltd must open its treasury gateway directly with a Tier 1 domestic bank; EMI rails may only support travel expense or treasury card spending after the underlying bank account has been approved, and must not be named beneficiary of inbound capital injections.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical in-branch attendance is not mandated by statute under the Companies Act 1994 or AML/CFT rules, but bank risk appetite usually requires at least one director or authorised signatory to complete a live video interview and electronic identity verification. Remote consular proxy opening is permitted in limited form: a notarised power of attorney can lodge the certified identity and corporate documents at a branch in New Zealand, but the ultimate beneficial owner and directors must still provide passport-level identity data and a source-of-wealth statement via recorded call or an approved electronic KYC vendor. Purely postal-based opening without any live verification is generally not available for cross-border corporate service entities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholders and directors lack New Zealand tax identification; the bank’s EDD team flags ownership opacity and tax-residency uncertainty.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Incorporation, constitution, register of directors and shareholders, beneficial-ownership chart, individual passports in certified/apostilled copy, IRD number application or taxpayer confirmation, six-month source-of-funds bank statements from the parent, notarised declarations of source of wealth, commercial references from shipowner clients, and board resolution authorising account opening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection into the escrow account is large relative to revenue and precedes a substantial crew payroll programme, creating an unexplained source-of-funds red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed crewing agency agreement with the vessel operator, proforma fee schedule and payroll register, commercial invoice and bank SWIFT confirmation, statutory declaration of source and purpose of funds, prior-year audited financial statements or management accounts, charter-party extract evidencing vessel income, and a projected cash-flow forecast explaining the capital need.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Crew roster contains seafarers or ultimate payees in OFAC/EU/UN-sanctioned jurisdictions or high-risk FATF-monitored countries, triggering autonomous sanctions and PEP screening.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete seafarer manifest with passport numbers and expiries, individual negative media/sanctions screening reports, PEP declarations, valid STCW certificates and seafarer employment contracts, proof of rights to work or transit visas, Maritime New Zealand manning-license certificate, and an internal sanctions-risk policy confirming prohibition on payments to blocked parties or vessels.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Frequent multi-currency payroll wires to overseas crew members are profiled as potentially unlicensed money transmission or currency conversion without a foreign-exchange dealer licence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: AML/CFT risk assessment, statutory crew recruitment licence from Maritime New Zealand, detailed payroll liability register showing gross/net wages and employer deductions, monthly reconciliation of escrow account versus payroll obligations, audit letter from an NZCA chartered accountant confirming that all payments are crew wages, and bank responses to prior monitoring alerts if any.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital must be routed via SWIFT MT103 from the non-resident shareholder or shipowner to the NZ Tier 1 bank account designated as the escrow/operational account. The wire should carry purpose code 'Current account - business services' for trade receivables or 'Foreign direct investment - equity capital' for capital injection. The beneficiary account description in the SWIFT field must contain the company's full legal name and tax ID to avoid name-checks; funds must not be labelled as salary or personal remittance. FX conversion from USD/EUR to NZD or from NZD to intended payroll currencies will be executed by the onshore bank as principal, with the bank issuing a client trade confirmation containing the agreed spot rate and settlement value. Capital verification is completed by maintaining a share register update, filing Companies Office annual returns, obtaining an NZCA accountant capital-verification certificate and retaining SWIFT MT103 confirmations. Foreign direct investment screening under the Overseas Investment Act 2005 is not ordinarily required for a crew recruitment service agency unless it acquires sensitive land, fishing quota or a materially strategic New Zealand business, and a legal waiver letter documenting this exemption should be kept in the bank file.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: SWIFT MT103 is the primary clearing rail for crew wages and trade disbursements as it provides beneficiary traceability and purpose codes such as 'SERV' for services and 'SALA' for actual salaries paid to seafarers. Commercial letters of credit may be used for vessel supplies and provisions or shipowner settlement guarantees, but are unsuitable for monthly multi-country payroll. Documentary collections may be used for unpaid invoice balances, crew boarding expense reimbursements and travel-clearing items. Multi-currency payroll will be run as a bank-hosted payroll sweep, converting NZD to USD/EUR/GBP/SGD at intraday rates and remitting to crew member bank accounts by MT103 or to licensed prepaid payroll card wallets. Payments to flagged jurisdictions will be blocked and routed to the sanctions officer for review; all payroll transactions must reconcile to the crewing contract, vessel name, crew visa number and seafarer discharge book reference.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable NZD/USD forward contracts with maturity up to 24 months via ANZ, ASB, BNZ or Westpac to hedge forecast crew payroll obligations
Cross-currency swaps (NZD/USD, NZD/GBP, NZD/EUR) used exclusively for matching future service-fee receivables and payroll liabilities
Plain vanilla FX swaps for working-capital conversion between operating currencies on a roll-forward basis

NDFs are legally permissible but market-depth is minimal for NZD because the currency is fully deliverable; any NDF used by a related treasury must be limited to non-NZD emerging-market exposures, not the NZD core

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies, MBIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than one calendar month after the anniversary date of incorporation, each year (s 209 of the Companies Act 1993). Example: incorporation on 18 March = due by 18 April.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of NZD 50 (about USD 30) after the due date; continued default results in a notice of removal and strike-off from the New Zealand Companies Register under ss 318-319 of the Companies Act 1993; directors also face fines of up to NZD 5,000 for failure to comply with annual return requirements.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Financial Statements and Auditor's Report Filing (for companies exceeding large or FMC reporting thresholds)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 20 working days after the date on which the financial statements are signed, or within 5 months after balance date for a 31 March balance date, whichever is earlier, in accordance with the Financial Reporting Act 2013 and s 209 of the Companies Act 1993.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file audited financial statements is an offence under the Financial Reporting Act 2013; fines up to NZD 50,000 for the company and NZD 10,000 for every director; the Registrar may also apply to the court for a compliance order or strike off the company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a standard 31 March balance date: 7 July following the balance date. For a non-standard balance date: on or before the 7th day of the month following the end of the seven-month period after the balance date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment penalty of 1% of unpaid tax immediately, 4% after 7 days, then 1% per month; use of money interest applied daily from the original due date; Inland Revenue may issue a demand, file a charging order, commence bankruptcy or compulsory winding-up, and directors may be personally liable under the Tax Administration Act 1994 for certain unpaid employer-related tax debts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due on or before the 28th day after the end of each prescribed GST period (monthly, two-monthly, or six-monthly). Mandatory registration applies if annual taxable turnover exceeds NZD 60,000 (approximately USD 36,500).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment penalty: 1% of unpaid GST immediately, 4% after 7 days, and 1% monthly thereafter; use of money interest accrues daily; failure to register or file may attract fines of NZD 1,000 for non-electronic filings and NZD 500 for electronic filings; continued non-payment triggers Inland Revenue debt collection and possible strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual filers: due 20 July after the tax year end; quarterly filers: due the 20th of the month following the end of each quarter.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties and use of money interest apply as for income tax; the employer remains liable for FBT; failure to file can incur penalties of up to NZD 1,000; continued default can lead to Inland Revenue enforcement including asset seizure and director liability if generated through payroll.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: AML/CFT Annual Report (if acting as a reporting entity under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department of Internal Affairs (AML/CFT Group) or designated supervisor
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after the end of the reporting entity's financial year; if the balance date is 31 March, due by 29 June.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to provide an annual report to the supervisor is an offence under the AML/CFT Act 2009; serious non-compliance can result in criminal penalties of imprisonment up to 2 years or a fine up to NZD 1,000,000 for an individual or NZD 5,000,000 for a company; civil penalties and compliance orders also apply.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Private Seafarer Recruitment and Placement Service (MLC 2006) Annual Confirmation / Certification Renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 30 days before the anniversary date of the certificate, or as specified in the certificate, under the Maritime Labour Convention 2006 and the Maritime Transport Act 1994.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Operating without a valid seafarer recruitment and placement certificate is a breach of the Maritime Transport Act 1994 and may result in licence suspension, refusal of vessel clearance, fines up to NZD 10,000 per incident, and removal from Maritime New Zealand's approved recruiter list.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Financial Reporting Act 2013, an independent certified CPA audit is legally mandatory if the company is: (1) a 'large company' where total assets exceed NZD 60 million at balance date AND total revenue exceeds NZD 30 million for the last two consecutive accounting periods; (2) an FMC reporting entity under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013; (3) a large overseas company carrying on business in New Zealand; (4) part of a large group where consolidated group assets exceed NZD 60 million and consolidated group revenue exceeds NZD 30 million; or (5) a company whose constitution, shareholder resolution, or shareholders holding 5% or more of voting rights require an audit under s 202 of the Companies Act 1993. Any entity below these thresholds is not compulsorily audited but may still elect to have a full audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand generally accepted accounting practice (NZ GAAP) as issued by the External Reporting Board (XRB). Tier 1: NZ IFRS (NZ equivalents of IFRS); Tier 2: NZ IFRS with reduced disclosures; Tier 3: NZ IFRS for SMEs (appropriate for small and medium companies with no public accountability and simple operations, such as a ship crew recruitment agency); Tier 4: simpler cash-based accounting for very small public sector entities. The Financial Reporting Act 2013 and the XRB A1 accounting standards framework govern the selection of the applicable framework.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand does not require a separate annual beneficial ownership return to the Companies Office. Under the AML/CFT Act 2009, a reporting entity, including a maritime crew agency if handling seafarer payroll or providing recruitment services, must adopt and implement a compliance programme that obtains and verifies beneficial ownership information at initial engagement, updates it whenever a material change occurs, and refreshes it at least annually. Shareholding transfers must be registered in the company's shareholder register within 30 days of application; changes in directors, shareholders, and registered office must also be reported to the Companies Office through the annual return or a notice of change within 20 working days of the change.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: AML/CFT beneficial ownership register (internal, where applicable)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 350 - 900 per annum, including the registered office, agent for service, secretarial handling, registry updates, and standard minute book maintenance.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 - 28,000 per annum for a full certified statutory audit prepared under NZ IFRS or NZ IFRS for SMEs, depending on transaction volume, payroll headcount, and organisational complexity.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No free-zone or patent-box regime in New Zealand. A 15% refundable Research & Development (R&D) tax credit is available on eligible R&D expenditure; R&D loss tax credits can be cashed out by qualifying start-ups. For a shipping crew recruitment agency, no preferential statutory rate applies; company income is taxed at 28% with imputation credits attaching to shareholder dividends.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 - Company Income Tax Return; filed electronically through the Inland Revenue myIR portal. Where cross-border related-party transactions exceed the disclosure threshold, attach IR833 - Transfer Pricing Disclosure Return through myIR.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; provisional tax is paid in three instalments during the income year, but no quarterly income tax return is required for a standard NZ limited company.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The IR4 is due on the 7th day of the 7th month after balance date. For a 31 March balance date the due date is 7 July; for a taxpayer represented by a registered tax agent the filing deadline may be extended to 31 March of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered entity details: legal name, IRD number, tax residence status, and major shareholder information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare the entity's place of central management and control. A New Zealand-incorporated company is tax-resident in New Zealand; a non-resident controlled company remains resident if incorporated here. If the board controls are exercised from a treaty jurisdiction, claim treaty residence only with a valid Tax Residency Certificate; NZ-sourced vessel-crewing income will still be taxable if a permanent establishment exists in New Zealand.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance date and duration of the income year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a 12-month period ending on a non-standard date, the statutory filing deadline moves accordingly. For a ship-crew recruitment agency, separately identify income from crew supply to foreign-flagged vessels: PAYE obligations arise for seafarers deriving employment income in New Zealand or on New Zealand coastal voyages; for foreign-flagged international voyages, source analysis under Income Tax Act 2007 sections YD 4 and YD 5 applies and the IR4 must be reconciled with the wage withholding position.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross income: commission fees, crew-management fees, payroll administration fees, disbursements recharged, and any ancillary maritime staffing revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include all income sourced in New Zealand. Non-resident companies are taxable on New Zealand-sourced income; if the company is resident in New Zealand, worldwide income is taxable. For a non-resident crew agency with no New Zealand permanent establishment, only crew management services physically performed in New Zealand are taxable; a mere offshore back-office arrangement cannot shift NZ-sourced fees abroad.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total deductible expenses: seafarer payroll, subcontractor crewing costs, insurance, certifications, international marketing, bank charges, legal and professional fees, and administrative overheads.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct only expenses incurred in deriving assessable income and substantiated by contemporaneous invoices. Intercompany management fees, crew payroll recharges, and shared IT/HR costs must satisfy the OECD benefit test and be priced at arm's length. Expenses paid to a non-resident parent for stewardship or duplicated shareholder activities are not deductible; excessive payments may be recharacterised as distributions or capital under Part D of the Income Tax Act 2007.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit or loss before tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply transfer pricing adjustments under sections GC 6 to GC 14 of the Income Tax Act 2007. If IRD adjusts the gross margin of the crew agency, this box is amended to reflect an arm's length result. No adjustment is required solely because the shareholder is non-resident; the amount must be independently benchmarked against comparable third-party crew-management agencies using appropriate profit level indicators.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after subtraction of available tax losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loss continuity requires more than 50% of shareholder continuity (49% same persons) under sections IA 5 and IB 1 of the Income Tax Act 2007. If the ownership of the NZ Ltd changed through a foreign investor's entry or exit, verify continuity at each relevant time; an ownership breach forfeits the loss carry-forward. Non-resident shareholders' imputation credits cannot be used to create a refund of NRWT.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax calculation: income tax on taxable income at 28%, plus credits for provisional tax paid, resident withholding tax, imputation credits, and foreign income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply New Zealand's foreign tax credit regime only for foreign taxes paid on foreign-sourced income included in Box 3. For an inbound non-resident parent, do not claim foreign tax credits for taxes paid by the parent on the NZ company's profits; those taxes are eliminated at the shareholder level via exemption or credit only if a DTA so provides. The ICA must be positive before any imputation credits are attached to dividends.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure schedule: related-party transactions, transfer pricing disclosure declaration, non-resident shareholder detail, NRWT reconciliation, and tax agent declaration.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If total cross-border related-party transactions exceed NZD 10 million, file IR833 and maintain a Master File and Local File. For dividends, interest, or royalties paid to non-residents, reconcile NRWT that must be withheld and remitted separately. Confirm whether DTA relief is claimed and hold the recipient's Tax Residency Certificate and beneficial ownership declaration. An unsupported treaty claim is a serious compliance red flag.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts an IRD late-filing penalty commencing at NZD 250 (increased to NZD 500 for medium/large taxpayers). Late payment penalties are 1% per month up to 10%, plus use-of-money interest under Part 7 of the Tax Administration Act 1994. Incorrect returns: a shortfall penalty of 20% for an unacceptable tax position and 40% for an abusive tax avoidance arrangement; evasion or similar offence under sections 143A-143B carries a maximum fine of NZD 250,000 for a company and imprisonment of up to 5 years for officers. Civil avoidance penalties are separate from prosecution.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% NRWT on dividends that are not fully imputed; 15% NRWT on fully imputed dividends paid to non-residents; DTA rates may reduce portfolio dividends to 15% and substantial-shareholding dividends to 5% or 0% depending on the treaty and shareholding threshold.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The payer must hold, before the relevant payment, a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the competent authority of the recipient's residence state, a signed beneficial ownership declaration that the recipient is not a nominee or conduit, and the recipient's foreign tax identification number. Where the domestic law requires, the non-resident must apply to the Inland Revenue for a certificate of exemption or reduced withholding determination before payment; a refund of excess NRWT may be obtained by filing an amended NRWT reconciliation and supplying the TRC plus full evidence of the transaction chain. The document package must be retained and produced on IRD request; for New Zealand treaties with no limitation-on-benefits article, the GAAR in section BG 1 of the Income Tax Act 2007 and the OECD principal-purpose test embed economic substance as a condition of relief.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: statutory NRWT is 15%, generally reduced to 10% under most New Zealand DTAs; the Approved Issuer Levy at 2% may replace NRWT on certain public-offered interest but is rarely available for intercompany debt. Royalties: statutory NRWT is 15%, commonly reduced to 10% under DTA royalty articles, with some treaties providing 5% for copyright or industrial royalties. For a crew-management agency, payments for the use of proprietary crew databases, software, or know-how are royalties; fees for administrative services are not royalties but are still subject to transfer pricing, GST, and potentially non-resident services withholding obligations.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: NZD 10,000,000 in aggregate cross-border related-party transactions per income year triggers the mandatory Transfer Pricing Disclosure Return (IR833); contemporaneous Master File and Local File documentation must be maintained to the OECD standard for any transaction above this threshold, and IRD may also request documentation for smaller intercompany contracts under its general information powers.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand does not have an Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) statute of the type used in offshore financial centres, but the general anti-avoidance rule in section BG 1, the specific anti-avoidance rules in sections GC 6-GC 14, and the limitation-on-benefits/principal-purpose test embedded in New Zealand's tax treaties require the crew agency to demonstrate real activity and core income-generating activities in New Zealand. A so-called contractor that only invoices commissions while the actual recruitment, payroll, and vessel-crew supervision are performed by non-resident group companies will be treated as having no economic substance; IRD may reattribute the income to the entity that performs the value-creating functions, require arm's length service fees, and deny treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Maritime payroll and withholding tax evasion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Misclassifying seafarer wages and crew payroll as offshore contractor payments to a foreign shell corporation, or routing salaries through a non-resident entity, to avoid New Zealand PAYE, ACC levies, and NRWT obligations for crew services rendered in respect of New Zealand coastal shipping or from a New Zealand permanent establishment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax Administration Act 1994 sections 141B and 141C impose a 20% shortfall penalty for an unacceptable tax position and a 40% shortfall penalty for an abusive tax avoidance arrangement, with use-of-money interest. Section 143A criminalises evasion with a company fine of up to NZD 250,000 and imprisonment of up to 5 years for the natural-person officers involved. The employer-level PAYE obligations are imposed under the PAYE rules in Schedule 4 of the Income Tax Act 2007, and a failure to account for withheld PAYE triggers director penalties under section 149A of the TAA.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced by statute: directors can be held jointly and severally liable for withheld PAYE and NRWT that the company deducted but failed to pay to the Commissioner. Civil asset-recovery proceedings may attach personal assets under the Proceeds of Crime Act 2009; the Commissioner may apply for a departure prohibition order under TAA sections 157A-157G, barring the director from leaving New Zealand until the tax debt is secured. Reckless trading liability under sections 135-136 of the Companies Act 1993 permits the Court to order a director to repay company losses, and fraudulent trading under section 380 of the Companies Act can lead to personal liability and criminal disqualification as a director.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer pricing documentation failure and base eroding intercompany fees
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying excessive management, marketing, or administrative fees to a related non-resident crewing-affiliate without sufficient functional analysis, failing to file IR833 when cross-border related-party transactions exceed NZD 10 million, and claiming deductions for services for which no benefit was received or that duplicate activities already performed by the New Zealand company.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Sections GC 6-GC 14 of the Income Tax Act 2007 empower the IRD to calculate the taxpayer's income at arm's length, reduce the amount of the deduction, and recharacterise the payment as a dividend or capital contribution. A failure to hold contemporaneous documentation reverses the burden of proof and exposes the company to a 40% abusive-tax-position shortfall penalty under TAA section 141C, plus shortfall interest. A false IR833 declaration is a tax refund/false statement offence under TAA section 143A, with fines of up to NZD 250,000 for companies.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who caused or permitted the false documentation may be personally assessed for the shortfall penalty under TAA section 141D when they materially contributed to the offending tax position without taking reasonable care. In insolvency settings, directors who continue the company while the tax debt is mounting are liable under the reckless trading provisions of the Companies Act 1993, and the Court can make a personal contribution order against directors' assets. Criminal conviction for dishonest transfer-pricing documents attracts imprisonment of up to 5 years, in addition to travel restrictions and director disqualification under company law.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Treaty shopping and sham DTA relief on profit repatriation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Interposing a third-country conduit, for example a Hong Kong, Singapore, or offshore intermediate company, that lacks beneficial ownership, premises, and employees, to route dividends, interest, or royalties away from New Zealand and obtain a reduced NRWT rate under a DTA that the ultimate owner could not directly enjoy.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Commissioner cancels the treaty benefit under the relevant DTA's beneficial-ownership, limitation-of-benefits, or principal-purpose test, and applies the general anti-avoidance rule in section BG 1. The under-withheld NRWT is collected at the statutory rate (30% dividends, 15% interest/royalties) with interest; a shortfall penalty of 40% applies for an abusive tax arrangement under TAA section 141C. Knowingly submitting false declarations to support the treaty claim is a criminal offence under TAA sections 143A-143B, with fines up to NZD 250,000 and 5 years' imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who arranged or participated in the conduit structure may be jointly liable for the company's withholding-tax shortfall; a court may pierce the corporate veil where the NZ Ltd and the conduit are a mere sham or façade. Civil liability includes asset restitution in favour of the Commissioner, personal accountability for company debts under the Companies Act 1993, a departure prohibition order for unpaid tax, and in serious cases conspiracy or dishonesty charges under the Crimes Act 1961 carrying imprisonment of up to 7 years.
